definition: Strict Type A: evidence explicitly names knees/hands as the active non-lying posture but final label remains positive.
Type B: evidence asserts lying/collapsed posture although source scenario/image is a stable non-lying posture.
Type C: support surface is materially misidentified.
Type D: another person is used as the target posture.
Type E: residual not covered above.
Audit dimension; not counted as strict Type A unless an explicit non-lying posture is named as the model conclusion.
